english.explanation: Let eG,eH be the identities of (G, ο) & (H, ∗) respectively. Then external direct product of G & H is a group (G × H, οp) with identity (eG, eH) Suppose (G, ο) and (H, ∗) are both abelian then in external direct product group (G × H, οp) we observe (g1, h1) οp (g2, h2) = (g1 ο g2, h1 ∗ h2) (by definition) = (g2 ο g1, h2 ∗ h1) (commutativity) = (g2, h2) οp (g1, h1) Thus, (G × H, οp) is abelian. Now, suppose that (G × H, οp) is abelian. Then (g1 ο g2, eH) = (g1 ο g2, eH ∗ eH) = (g1, eH) οp (g2, eH) = (g2, eH) οp (g1, eH) (commutativity) = (g2 ο g1, eH ∗ eH) = (g2 ο g1, eH) Thus, g1 ο g2 = g2 ο g1 and (G, ο) is abelian. Similarly, (H, ∗) is abelian. Therefore, if (G, ο) and (H, ∗) are two groups then external direct product (G × H, οp) is abelian if and only if both (G, ο) and (H, ∗) are abelian.
